寓書房玄齡 means he sent (entrusted) a letter to Fang Xuanling, which Junkuo then opened (s0302); it does not mean he was lodging with Fang. The literal field has the same error.

For this Xuandao was banished to Xi Prefecture (Xizhou); soon after he was promoted to prefect of Changzhou, where his rule was clear and spare; the throne issued a decree of praise and granted him silk.

The Emperor admired his loyalty, allowed him to escort the prince to Shunyang Pavilion, and left in tears.
The Emperor admired his loyalty, allowed him to escort the prince to Shunyang Pavilion, where Silian took his leave in tears.
泣辭去 refers to Yao Silian taking leave of the prince in tears, not the emperor; the literal field ("took leave in tears") leaves the subject ambiguous.

洗馬 (太子洗馬) is the office Librarian of the Heir Apparent, not a "cavalry escort"; the literal field has the same error.

He received five hundred bolts of variegated silk and was promoted to general gentleman of comprehensive directness and regular cavalry.
He received five hundred bolts of variegated silk and was promoted to Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary with Direct Access.
通直散騎常侍 is the single office Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary with Direct Access; the rendering garbles it. The literal field has the same error.
Small wonder Taizong honored him so, as the inscription records.
Small wonder Taizong honored and distinguished him.
尊表 means to honor and distinguish; there is no inscription in the source. The literal field has the same error.

The empress was delighted; he was made acting vice minister of the Celestial Office, then promoted to left assistant of the Department of Literary Glory and joint manager of affairs with the Phoenix Pavilion and Luan Terrace (chief minister).
同鳳閣鸞臺平章事 is the chief-minister designation, not a "co-drafter"; the literal field has the same error.

納言 here is the Zhou-era name of the Director of the Chancellery, not a "chief speaker"; the literal field has the same error.
Ji Kang was put to death, yet Shan Tao remained loyal unto death.
Ji Kang was put to death, yet his son Ji Shao died for loyalty.
紹 is Ji Shao (嵇紹), Ji Kang's son, not Shan Tao; the literal field has the same error.

知反流徙者什八以上 means that over eighty percent were exiled for knowing of the rebellion, not that the exiles "knew themselves innocent"; the literal field has the same error.
He was appointed Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, concurrently serving as Left Subordinate to the Heir Apparent.
He was appointed Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent, concurrently serving as Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
太子詹事 is Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent and 左庶子 is Left Mentor; "Grand Mentor" (太子太傅) is a different office. The literal field has the same errors.
When the other palace officials were all punished, Ting alone was promoted to Right Regular Attendant of the Cavalry and appointed Director of the Secretariat.
When the other palace officials were all punished, Ting alone was promoted to Right Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and appointed Director of the Palace Library.
秘書監 is Director of the Palace Library, not of the Secretariat (中書); 右散騎常侍 is Right Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary. The literal field has the same errors.
The posts he had held—Prefect of Dingzhou and various ministerial offices—were subsequently filled in succession by Shu, it is said.
The posts he had held—Prefect of Dingzhou and various ministerial offices—had been held in succession by him and Shu, one after the other, it is said.
皆與璹相繼 means Ting held these posts in succession with his elder brother Shu, who had held them first; the rendering reverses the sequence. The literal field has the same error.
At the beginning of the Wude reign he was appointed Attendant of Daily Records, then promoted to Assistant Director of the Secretariat.
At the beginning of the Wude reign he was appointed Attendant of Daily Records, then promoted to Assistant Director of the Palace Library.
秘書丞 is Assistant Director of the Palace Library, not of the Secretariat; the literal field has the same error.

Thereupon the Emperor issued an edict appointing Director of the Secretariat Xiao Yu, Supervising Secretary Wang Jingye, and Compilation Officer Yin Wenli to compile the Wei history; Director of the Secretariat Feng Deyi and Attendant Yan Shigu for the Sui history; Chief Judge Cui Shanwei, Secretariat Attendant Kong Shao'an, and Groom of the Heir Apparent Xiao Deyan for the Liang history; Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent Pei Ju, Bureau Director Zu Xiaosun, and Assistant Director of the Palace Library Wei Zheng for the Qi history; Director of the Palace Library Dou Jin, Supervising Secretary Ouyang Xun, and Literary Scholar Yao Silian for the Chen history; and Director of the Chancellery Chen Shuda, Grand Astrologer Yu Jian, and Defen for the Zhou history.

The literal field has the same errors.

He was appointed Right Subordinate to the Heir Apparent.
He was appointed Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
太子右庶子 is the Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent; the literal field has the same rendering.
He was made Deputy Director of the Secretariat.
He was made Vice Director of the Palace Library.
秘書少監 is Vice Director of the Palace Library, not of the Secretariat; the literal field has the same error.

At the beginning of the Yonghui reign he again served as Vice Minister of Rites and Academician of the Hongwen Library, overseeing revision of the National History, and was then appointed Minister of Rites.

At the beginning of the Yonghui reign he again served as Vice Minister of Rites and Academician of the Hongwen Library, overseeing revision of the National History, and was then appointed Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
太常卿 is Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, not Minister of Rites (禮部尚書); the literal field has the same error.

Early on the Emperor had conquered the realm by force of arms and turned to learning only later. He often composed prose and poetry himself; his literary taste was rich and ornate, his vision lofty and bold.
多屬文賦詩 means he often composed (屬文) prose and poetry; it does not mean he commissioned others. The literal field has the same error ("entrusted others").
His father Lan served the Sui as a Secretariat academician.
His father Lan served the Sui as an academician of the Palace Library.
秘書學士 belongs to the Palace Library (秘書省), not the Secretariat; the literal field has the same error.
For organizing the National History he was promoted to Gentleman Consultant for Ceremonies and enfeoffed Viscount of Yuhang County.
For organizing the National History he was promoted to Gentleman Consultant for Ceremonies and enfeoffed Baron of Yuhang County.
縣男 is Baron, not Viscount (縣子); the literal field has the same error.
His son Cong served under Empress Wu as Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel and a Grand Chancellor of Tongfeng Pavilion and Luantai.
His son Cong served under Empress Wu as Vice Minister of the Celestial Office (Personnel) and joint manager of affairs with the Phoenix Pavilion and Luan Terrace (chief minister).
同鳳閣鸞臺平章事 means joint manager of affairs with the Phoenix Pavilion and Luan Terrace; 同 is not part of a place name "Tongfeng". The literal field has the same misparse.
Linghu Tan was a fifth-generation descendant of Linghu Defen.
Linghu Huan was a fifth-generation descendant of Linghu Defen.
令狐峘 is Linghu Huan (峘 read huan), not "Tan"; the literal field has the same misreading. The name is repaired in every unit of this chunk where it occurs.

Yang Guan often visited him when still unknown; Huan was erudite and eloquent.

When compiling the 《Veritable Records of Emperor Xuanzong》 he found the Diary Notes lost and scattered, so Huan pieced together edicts and proclamations to preserve what remained of the reign.
令狐峘 is Linghu Huan (峘 read huan), not "Tan"; the literal field has the same misreading. The name is repaired in every unit of this chunk where it occurs.
Tan remonstrated: "I have read Liu Xiang of Han on the warning about tombs, and good historians have mournfully sighed over it.
Huan remonstrated: "I have read Liu Xiang of Han on the warning about tombs, and good historians have mournfully sighed over it.
令狐峘 is Linghu Huan (峘 read huan), not "Tan"; the literal field has the same misreading. The name is repaired in every unit of this chunk where it occurs.

While in the Ministry of Personnel Huan relied on the support of Minister Liu Yan.

That day Huan memorialized: "The Chancellor pressured me with a private favor—if I complied I would betray Your Majesty, if I refused he would destroy me."

The prefect Tian Dun had been Huan's student though they had never met; he now came to welcome him and gave him half his salary for support.
